video_title: A Worm With 302 Neurons Inspired Their Architecture — Ramin Hasani, Liquid AI
gist: Liquid AI's CEO traces the company from C. elegans-inspired continuous-time neural networks at Vienna and MIT to a hardware-aware architecture-search engine (STAR) that generates the LFM model family, and then lays out the commercial reality: on-device deployments with Mercedes-Benz and AMD, over a billion monthly Shopify requests, ~40M open-weight downloads, and a beta self-serve customization platform. The strategic thesis is that inference tokens are today's 90% of the market while 'customization tokens' are the next wave, and that architecture bias should increase as models shrink and disappear as they scale.

themes.theme: C. elegans origins and the recurrence-vs-attention tradeoff

insights.claim: Liquid AI's architecture lineage began ~12 years ago at Vienna University of Technology with an attempt to model how two biological neurons exchange information using first-order differential equations, producing 'liquid time-constant' neural networks.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: The company's moat is a decade-plus of continuous-time dynamical-systems research, not a recent transformer fork — relevant when assessing defensibility against frontier labs adding alternative-architecture teams.

insights.claim: The team deliberately chose the C. elegans worm over the human brain as a model organism because its 302 neurons are non-spiking (electrotonic), making them mathematically continuous and differentiable, so backpropagation can be applied directly.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: The 'worm-inspired' branding is a literal technical constraint (differentiability), not marketing — a useful test of whether biologically-inspired AI claims are substantive.
insights.quote: its neurons behave very similar to artificial neurons they don't they don't spike

insights.claim: C. elegans controls 95 muscle cells with only 302 neurons — which in 2016-2017 outperformed any robotic control system then available — and this compute-efficiency-per-neuron result is what pushed Liquid toward intelligence at the smallest unit of compute.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: Establishes the founding bet — efficiency per parameter rather than scale — which is the same bet now monetized in on-device deployments.
insights.quote: with 302 neurons it could control 95 muscle cells better than any robotic systems that we had on the planet

insights.claim: MIT's Daniela Rus recruited the Vienna team to MIT in 2017, and Liquid's four founders (Hasani, Matthias, Rus, Alexander Amini) have worked together on continuous-time learning systems since then.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: Founding-team continuity since 2017 and MIT robotics pedigree are material to diligence on a company selling into automotive and industrial OEMs.

insights.claim: The transformer's advantage is that it is an unbiased architecture reducible to matrix multiplications, which won the 'hardware lottery' on GPUs — not that it is theoretically superior at sequence modeling.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: If the substrate changes (photonics, NPUs, custom silicon), the transformer's structural advantage weakens — the core option value in alternative-architecture companies.
insights.quote: They are basically matrix multiplications and you can actually like scale them like it's the hardware lottery

insights.claim: Recurrent architectures have sub-quadratic-to-linear compute cost as context grows versus attention's quadratic cost, but that efficiency is purely theoretical unless the nonlinear recurrence can be parallelized on hardware.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: Explains why paper-level FLOP advantages of RNN/SSM alternatives have repeatedly failed to translate into shipped frontier models.

insights.claim: State space models are the linearized version of recurrent neural networks: linearization buys parallel-scan scalability but destroys the nonlinear parameter relationships that carry expressivity.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: A compact mental model for evaluating any 'linear attention' claim: ask what expressivity was traded for the parallelism.
insights.quote: there's no free launch in computer science right so when you linearize a a complicated dynamics you're losing expressivity

insights.claim: Pure state space models struggle to learn long-context dependencies in language and fall short of transformers in expressive power, which is why Liquid builds hybrids rather than betting on a single alternative operator.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: Supports a hybrid-architecture rather than transformer-replacement investment thesis in the alternative-architecture category.
insights.quote: they can compute really efficiently but they cannot they express very efficiently

insights.claim: Ten years after the transformer paper, attention will remain a necessary component of general-purpose architectures for a long time, but it is only one component alongside hardware-awareness, embodiment and adaptivity.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: A leading alternative-architecture founder explicitly not predicting the transformer's death — tempering expectations for a discontinuous architecture regime change.
insights.quote: Attention is definitely one element that you need

themes.theme: STAR architecture search as the real product

insights.claim: Liquid's founding move three years ago was to assemble inventors of competing alternative architectures (hyena hierarchy, state space models via Stanford's Jimmy Smith, liquid networks) in one place and build a meta-search system over the operator space instead of betting on one architecture.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: Reframes Liquid as an architecture-search platform rather than a single-architecture bet, which materially changes its obsolescence risk.
insights.quote: let's build a meta AI system that searches through the operation space

insights.claim: The STAR search optimizes four objectives simultaneously: no quality sacrifice versus a pure transformer across ~100 criteria, minimum memory consumption, minimum latency, and maximum compute speed — conditioned on the target deployment chip.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: The objective function is the productized asset; any buyer of an efficiency-first model should ask which of these four was actually traded.
insights.quote: Minimizing the memory consumption, minimizing latency and maximizing the speed of computation

insights.claim: Each LFM generation is an output of the same recursive architecture-search system with new operators added as they are invented: LFM1 was a mixed mess of convolution, attention and liquid operators, while LFM2 was optimized specifically for CPUs.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: Model releases are search outputs rather than hand-designed artifacts, implying a faster and more mechanical improvement cadence than competitors' manual tuning.

insights.claim: LFM2's shipped architecture is roughly 80% double-gated 1D convolutions plus about 20% grouped-query attention, deliberately simple so it runs fast and at high quality on CPUs.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: A concrete, checkable architecture spec — a convolution-dominant hybrid beating transformers on CPU is the clearest evidence of the search system working.
insights.quote: So the architecture is basically 80% doublegated convolutions you know 1D convolutions plus some uh group query attention basically 20% of query.

insights.claim: Liquid is a from-scratch foundation model lab running its own scaling laws across models from tens of millions to 70 billion parameters, currently shipping LFM2.5 with LFM3 next, adding quality, stability and latency control.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: 70B-scale internal scaling runs signal real pre-training capex and ambitions beyond the small-model niche the company is known for.
insights.quote: We scale these models from tens of millions of parameters now to 70 billion parameters.

insights.claim: Because the architecture search is hardware-aware, silicon companies designing next-generation NPUs are the most natural customers — they can put unreleased hardware in the loop to derive the optimal computation graph for their chip.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: A high-value, sticky wedge into semiconductor roadmaps that is far more defensible than selling small models; watch for silicon-vendor partnerships as the leading indicator.
insights.quote: our architecture search is hardware aware

themes.theme: On-device economics and the cloud/device split

insights.claim: Roughly 300-400 million AI PCs ship annually, of which about 100 million are AMD-powered, and Liquid is working with AMD to run LFMs locally on those laptops.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: Sizes the on-device inference TAM and names AMD as the distribution channel — a per-device licensing model scales with laptop unit volumes, not token volumes.
insights.quote: 300 million AI PCs are getting generated onu on the planet like every year

insights.claim: On current flagship phones with Apple Intelligence or Galaxy AI, about 90% of AI calls still go to the cloud and only 10% run on device, because on-device models are not yet powerful or reliable enough to absorb cloud use cases.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: Quantifies the addressable shift: every point of that 90% moved on-device is cloud inference revenue displaced and OEM margin created.
insights.quote: 90% of the calls are going to the cloud right so these are 90% goes to the cloud 10% on the device

insights.claim: The primary driver for OEMs moving AI on-device is raw cost — serving free intelligence to hundreds of millions or billions of clients from the cloud is prohibitive, so on-device inference is straightforward margin creation.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: Frames on-device AI as a COGS decision rather than a privacy story, which makes adoption far less discretionary and more durable through budget cycles.

insights.claim: A second on-device use case is a local privacy filter that intelligently strips sensitive data from prompts before they are sent to cloud agents like ChatGPT or Claude Code.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: Identifies a new software layer sitting between enterprise endpoints and frontier APIs — a category likely to attract both startups and endpoint-security incumbents.

insights.claim: Getting a model to production quality on a device is far harder than downloading an open-source model and porting it: it requires thermal control and managing model behavior drift in long context, learned over two and a half years of production cycles.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: The stated moat against commoditization by open weights — benchmark parity is not deployment parity, which is why OEMs pay licenses instead of self-serving.

insights.claim: Liquid's in-car multimodal model for Mercedes-Benz is about 600 megabytes, connects to cameras and voice, and is small enough to be pushed to every car via over-the-air update.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: Model size small enough for OTA distribution changes the automotive AI update cycle from hardware-bound to software-bound.
insights.quote: so this model itself is about 600 megabyte

insights.claim: The first at-scale Mercedes-Benz deployment lands this year across all North American Generation 3 cars, running on a chip costing roughly $100.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: A near-term, verifiable milestone and a bill-of-materials datapoint showing production AI does not require premium automotive silicon.
insights.quote: this is running on a on a chip that is probably 100 bucks

insights.claim: Shopify runs Liquid foundation models in private production deployments across merchant- and consumer-facing surfaces, including search in the Shop app, and that single Shopify workload now exceeds a billion requests per month with exponential growth.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: A billion+ monthly requests from one customer is hard evidence of production-grade reliability at consumer scale, not a pilot.
insights.quote: we are exponentially at over a billion uh request per month

insights.claim: Liquid's open-weight models have surpassed 40 million cumulative downloads at roughly 1.5 million per week, spanning 100 million to 24 billion parameters with mixture-of-experts at the larger end and audio/vision/text in and audio/text out.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: Download velocity is the top-of-funnel metric for a licensing business — a checkable public proxy for developer mindshare against Qwen/Gemma-class small models.
insights.quote: They have an overall over 40 millions of downloads and we have like 1.5 about 1.5 million downloads per week.

insights.claim: Liquid monetizes through paid design-partner engagements with an embedded applied ML team, converting into recurring per-year, per-device license fees, with service cost falling for each subsequent customer in a vertical once the first solution is built.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: A services-to-license margin ramp per vertical — gross margin should expand sharply after the anchor customer in each industry.

themes.theme: Customization tokens as the next monetization wave

insights.claim: About 90% of the current AI market is inference tokens sold by frontier labs and inference providers like Fireworks, but the next wave of value will accrue to monetizing 'customization tokens' as good open base models proliferate.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: An explicit call on where the next decacorns form — a screen for investing in customization/training-infrastructure startups over pure inference resellers.
insights.quote: right now like 90% of the market is around inference tokens

insights.claim: Customization should be defined as the full depth from pre-training through mid-training, post-training, data generation, RL and inference — not merely post-training — and the winners will let agents run that loop recursively so customers own their own intelligence.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: A broader definition than most 'fine-tuning platform' pitches; useful for judging which customization startups are actually addressing the full stack.

insights.claim: Companies named as riding the customization wave include Reflection, Thinking Machines, trajectory-style startups, and Jeff Dean's newly started lab, several already at decacorn valuations.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: A working comp set for the customization category, with the caveat that valuations already embed the thesis.

insights.claim: Liquid has a self-serve model-development platform in beta designed to sit inside the customer's own agentic harness as tools, rather than as another UI, so a developer's coding agent can walk through building and deploying a production-grade LFM.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: Distribution-as-tools rather than as a dashboard is the emerging pattern for AI developer products; a live example to watch for conversion from services to product revenue.

insights.claim: Static evals become obsolete once a model is in production because incoming data distribution shifts, so continuously evolving systems — not one-off eval-gated releases — are required.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: The argument for why human-in-the-loop and continual-learning tooling is a durable spend line rather than a one-time deployment cost.
insights.quote: Static evals are going to become obsolete.

insights.claim: Across roughly 200 Fortune 500 engagements, about 80% of enterprise AI proofs-of-concept never reach production, leaving mature enterprises exhausted and defaulting back to cloud solutions.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: An 80% PoC failure rate from a vendor with 200 F500 touchpoints is a caution flag for enterprise-AI revenue forecasts and a demand driver for self-serve tooling.
insights.quote: we worked probably with 200 of the Fortune 500 companies

insights.claim: Vibe coding has spread virally inside mature organizations, but roughly 90% of the tokens consumed produce no attributable value, which is itself creating enterprise demand for cost control and self-serve platforms.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: If enterprises conclude most coding-agent token spend is waste, inference demand growth from that segment is more fragile than headline usage suggests.
insights.quote: you will again end up with 90% of these tokens are useless tokens

insights.claim: Hasani defines true sovereign AI as every enterprise — and eventually every individual — owning their own model development and deployment, rather than the geopolitical national-compute framing.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: Reframes sovereign AI as a per-enterprise and per-person product category, which is a much larger market than national compute programs.
insights.quote: this is kind of the true meaning of sovereign AI

themes.theme: Design laws: bias scales inversely with model size

insights.claim: Architecture search across scaling-law runs shows that larger general-purpose models require less architectural bias, while in the small-model regime under memory constraints (e.g. 8GB) adding feedback loops and structural complexity yields more expressive dynamics.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: A design law that predicts which architectural tricks will and will not survive scaling — directly applicable to judging small-model startups' claims.
insights.quote: the more biases you add to the system the more expressive dynamics you get in the larger scale you remove those biases

insights.claim: LFM2 deliberately omits fashionable operators like gated delta nets in favor of plain 1D convolutions, on the principle that unbiased, unstructured operators scale better.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: A vote against operator complexity as a differentiator, consistent with the transformer's own simplicity advantage.

insights.claim: Layer looping is another form of architectural bias, which is why it helps at small scale and fades at large scale, and it also lacks an infrastructure fit because current GPU infrastructure is optimized for parallel matrix multiplication.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: Ties architecture viability back to infrastructure economics: techniques without kernel support will underperform regardless of theoretical merit.

insights.claim: Architecture choice should be matched to data modality: continuous-time systems, SSMs and RNNs are highly effective on audio and time-series data below roughly 20 billion parameters but perform poorly on text.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: Explains why SSM startups cluster in voice, and suggests voice-AI infrastructure is where non-transformer architectures win commercially first.
insights.quote: they're very effective in audio, but on text, they suck

insights.claim: Foundation model innovation should be decomposed into three separable classes — model architecture, learning algorithm (autoregressive, diffusion, world modeling), and data processing — so world models are an algorithmic choice that can be applied on top of an LFM architecture rather than a distinct architecture family.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: Deflates much of the 'action models and world models are fundamentally different' marketing in robotics, a useful filter for robotics-foundation-model claims.

insights.claim: World modeling extracts a different set of physical primitives than next-token prediction, and which learning algorithm unlocks the ChatGPT moment for robots remains an open question on the algorithmic rather than architectural side.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: A named, unresolved bottleneck — the robotics breakthrough is framed as algorithmic, not compute- or architecture-limited.

insights.claim: Liquid deliberately paused a robotics vertical from day one because production robotics requires verification, validation and regulatory approval, which delays go-to-market — opting instead for a horizontal intelligence layer sold to OEMs.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: A founder with deep robotics pedigree explicitly avoiding robotics on GTM grounds is a caution signal for robotics-first startup timelines.
insights.quote: robotics has been something that we deliberately kind of put it on pause day one

insights.claim: Liquid now considers it a good time to pursue robotics seriously because its models have matured and it has more control over data, post-training and customization for specific applications.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: A forward-looking signal on timing for industrial robotics foundation models from a player that has been waiting deliberately.

insights.claim: Liquid's vision-language models are already deployed for vision-action and instruction-following on modular industrial robots with partners including Roboto-style integrators and Gbionics in Italy, alongside AMD, focused on factories rather than humanoids.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: Industrial monitoring and instruction-following are shipping today while humanoids are not — the near-term revenue pocket in embodied AI.

insights.claim: A 7B-class model trained with world modeling can encode useful internal physical knowledge without being able to emit high-fidelity video, so small video-out models should be judged on representation quality rather than generation quality.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: Sets realistic expectations for small multimodal models targeting industrial grounding versus entertainment-grade generation.

themes.theme: Substrate bets, ecosystems and open questions

insights.claim: Photonics could be the breakthrough medium for alternative architectures because speed-of-light serial computation would remove the parallelization constraint that forces researchers to linearize nonlinear dynamical systems, and more broadly the substrate hosting intelligence determines which architectures are possible — natural intelligence runs on carbon, current AI on silicon.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: Identifies the specific mechanism by which photonics would matter — unlocking nonlinear recurrence — and links semiconductor/medium innovation directly to model-architecture innovation.
insights.quote: intelligence is a property of carbon

insights.claim: Quantum computing's main impact on AI would be on search — the parameter-space search currently approximated by gradient descent — rather than on most other bottlenecks, and a 2017 IBM engineer's own estimate for broad usability was 2035.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: Narrows quantum's AI relevance to optimization/search and sets a long timeline, useful for discounting quantum-AI narratives.
insights.quote: I think the only thing that it changes like massively it would be search

insights.claim: Most on-device inference engines that try to be hardware-general end up worse than llama.cpp, so ecosystem lock-in to a single hardware stack is what makes such platforms succeed — a pattern expected to apply to Mojo now that Modular has been acquired by Qualcomm.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: A blunt read on the compiler/kernel layer: bet on locked-in ecosystems, not on universal abstraction layers.
insights.quote: all of them are worse if you dig in they're worse than the original llama CPP

insights.claim: Liquid deliberately stays on the most native platform closest to the hardware rather than adopting new abstraction layers, having already switched from JAX to PyTorch, on the principle that ecosystem always wins and this is structurally unfair to new entrants.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: A direct headwind assessment for any new AI compiler, framework or runtime startup regardless of technical quality.
insights.quote: ecosystem always wins. You know it's it's just really brutal answer. It's not it's not fair to new entrance.

insights.claim: Hasani says he has heard that SSI is working on architectures similar to the original liquid neural network ideas, and assumes every frontier lab including Anthropic and OpenAI has teams investing heavily in alternative architectures.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: If frontier labs are internally pursuing continuous-time architectures, the alternative-architecture category is validated but also crowded by better-capitalized players.
insights.quote: I know that I've heard that SSI is also working very on the similar architectures to the original ideas of liquid neural networks

insights.claim: The largely unexplored frontier is adaptability — combining forward and backward passes at the same time so models adapt on the go, beyond in-context learning's pseudo-backprop at test time.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: Names the specific next architectural generation to watch, and distinguishes it from in-context learning, which he considers only a partial substitute.

insights.claim: Beyond single-model architecture, cognitive architectures composed of many small units of compute — neurons, LFMs or small models bundled into systems of systems — are a distinct direction from atom-level architecture innovation.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: Suggests small-model efficiency compounds in multi-agent systems, where per-unit inference cost dominates total system cost.

insights.claim: Liquid's current research agenda is massively multimodal training across all modalities simultaneously, longer-horizon reasoning for reliable on-device assistants, a dedicated efficiency department spanning kernels to RL infrastructure, and DNA foundation models exploiting long-context, small-vocabulary sequences.
insights.speaker: Ramin Hasani (CEO, Liquid AI)
insights.so_what: DNA sequence modeling is a natural, under-contested adjacency for long-context dynamical architectures — a possible second act beyond edge devices.
